source_version: Theory of Computing15(2019),Article17; final publisher source December17,2019
title: Approximate-majority gap between parity formulas and monotone circuits

standard_prerequisites.name: Boolean circuits/formulas, probabilistic polynomials and elementary concentration
standard_prerequisites.statement: Original approximate-majority convention and all local approximation, bias amplification and circuit layers retained.
standard_prerequisites.use: No collector reproof of cited standard polynomial-degree lower bounds; no deterministic-explicit upgrade of the original randomized circuit construction.

core_obligations: The authors pair a depth-sensitive probabilistic-polynomial approximation of parity formulas with a randomized layered monotone-circuit construction whose bias amplification and concentration are controlled through all depths. The complete approximation and circuit-construction arguments are retained, rather than quoting either main bound as free background. Both bounds form one approximate-majority separation object; the resulting class-separation corollaries are not extra counts.
